context: The prompt requests merging the 'CI/CD & DevOps' and 'Deployment Strategy' categories in the Technical Design schema into a single 'Deployment' category. This questionnaire clarifies implementation decisions about how to combine the two existing categories, which have separate sets of questions and potentially overlapping content.

questions.question-text: What should be the new category ID for the merged 'Deployment' category?

options.label: Keep 'DeploymentStrategy' ID and extend it
options.pros: Minimal disruption to existing answered questions with 'DeploymentStrategy' prefix, simpler migration path for existing data, maintains existing question IDs that start with DS_
options.cons: The ID is longer and more specific than the new broader category name 'Deployment', may be misleading since it now includes CI/CD content

options.label: Use 'CICD_DevOps' ID and extend it
options.pros: Reflects that CI/CD content is being included, maintains existing question IDs that start with CD_
options.cons: The ID doesn't match the new 'Deployment' category name at all, confusing for users, harder to understand the category scope from the ID

options.label: Create new 'Deployment' ID
options.pros: Clean naming that perfectly matches the new category name, clear break from the old structure, semantically correct, easier to understand
options.cons: Requires migrating or renaming all existing question IDs, more complex migration logic, potential data loss if not handled carefully

questions.recommendation-rationale: 'DeploymentStrategy' is the most appropriate ID to keep because: (1) deployment strategy is the broader concept that naturally encompasses CI/CD practices, (2) it minimizes disruption to existing data, and (3) it keeps the question ID prefix 'DS_' which is more intuitive than 'CD_' for a category called 'Deployment'.

questions.question-text: How should questions from both categories be organized in the merged category?

options.label: Place all CI/CD & DevOps questions first, then all Deployment Strategy questions
options.pros: Preserves original grouping, easier to implement, clear separation of concerns, users familiar with old structure can find questions easily
options.cons: May not provide the most logical flow, related questions might be far apart, doesn't take advantage of the merge to improve organization

options.label: Interleave questions logically by topic (e.g., CI tools, CD practices, deployment models, etc.)
options.pros: Better user experience with logical flow, related questions grouped together, takes advantage of merge to improve structure, more cohesive category
options.cons: More complex implementation, requires careful analysis of question relationships, may disrupt familiar ordering for existing users

options.label: Keep all Deployment Strategy questions first, then add CI/CD & DevOps questions
options.pros: Maintains the 'deployment' focus at the beginning which matches category name, straightforward implementation
options.cons: CI/CD questions at the end may seem like an afterthought, doesn't optimize for logical flow, may create confusion about scope

questions.recommendation-rationale: Placing CI/CD & DevOps questions first makes sense because: (1) CI/CD represents the pipeline and automation infrastructure that enables deployment, (2) it follows a natural progression from build/integration to deployment/delivery, (3) it's easier to implement and verify, and (4) it maintains clear boundaries between the original category content for easier troubleshooting.

questions.question-text: How should the merged category description be written?

options.label: Combine both original descriptions: 'Continuous integration, continuous delivery, pipelines, automation, IaC, environments, release strategy, testing, governance, release orchestration, deployment models, rollbacks, approvals, progressive delivery'
options.pros: Comprehensive coverage of all topics, nothing is lost from original descriptions, users understand full scope immediately
options.cons: Very long and somewhat redundant (pipelines, automation, IaC appear in both), harder to read, may feel overwhelming

options.label: Write a new concise description that captures the essence: 'End-to-end delivery: CI/CD pipelines, automation, infrastructure as code, deployment strategies, release orchestration, and operational governance'
options.pros: Clean and professional, removes redundancy, easier to read, covers all essential topics, flows logically from development to deployment to operations
options.cons: Requires careful wording to ensure nothing important is omitted, slightly more subjective than simply combining existing text

options.label: Use only the Deployment Strategy description since it's the target category: 'Release orchestration, deployment models, automation, rollbacks, approvals, pipelines, IaC, progressive delivery'
options.pros: Simpler, focuses on the category name, shorter description
options.cons: Loses explicit mention of CI/CD, testing, and governance aspects, may confuse users about whether CI/CD content belongs here

questions.recommendation-rationale: A new concise description is recommended because it: (1) eliminates redundancy from the two original descriptions, (2) presents a clear, logical flow from integration through deployment to operations, (3) explicitly includes both CI/CD and deployment aspects to clarify the merged scope, and (4) is professional and easy to understand while being comprehensive.

questions.question-text: Should question IDs from the CI/CD & DevOps category be renamed when merged?

options.label: Keep original question IDs unchanged (CD_ prefix from CI/CD & DevOps, DS_ prefix from Deployment Strategy)
options.pros: No data migration needed, existing answered questions remain valid, simpler implementation, backward compatible
options.cons: Inconsistent ID prefixes within one category (CD_ and DS_), may confuse users about which category a question belongs to

options.label: Rename all CI/CD & DevOps question IDs to use DS_ prefix to match Deployment Strategy
options.pros: Consistent ID prefix across entire merged category, cleaner structure, clearer category ownership
options.cons: Requires data migration for existing answered questions, more complex implementation, risk of losing existing user selections if migration fails

options.label: Rename all question IDs to use a new 'D_' (Deployment) prefix
options.pros: Perfect alignment with new category name, fresh start with clear naming, most semantically correct
options.cons: Requires migrating both sets of existing questions, highest implementation complexity, greatest risk of data loss

questions.recommendation-rationale: Keeping original question IDs is recommended because: (1) it preserves all existing answered questions without requiring migration, (2) it's the safest approach with no risk of data loss, (3) while the mixed prefixes (CD_ and DS_) are slightly inconsistent, they actually help users identify the origin of each question, and (4) the implementation is straightforward with minimal risk.
